intent: Second integration pass after owner rejected pasted-on appearance; rebuild physical housings and shared UI material language around approved poster wordmark.

edits.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Redesign and art-direct the branding integration of this portrait game menu.
IMAGE 1 is an unsuccessful first attempt at putting the poster logo into the toy-console home screen. IMAGE 2 is the authoritative logo design. The user rejected IMAGE 1 because the logo looks pasted on. Solve that visual design problem; produce a visibly revised integrated design, not another logo substitution.

Preserve the exact poster wordmark identity: HUMAN RESOURCES on two lines in cream custom slanted angular letters, narrow coral offset sides, strong H and R shapes, small cobalt saucer / mint triangular beam in the A, mint sweeping underline. Keep its letter spacing and proportions. BUT interpret it as a physical manufactured component of this toy UI, with the same lighting/material realism as the controls.
SPECIFIC NEW HEADER DESIGN:
- Completely replace the old top casing. Remove the tall empty triangular crest, ribbed speaker grille and spindly orange antennae. Those belonged to the old logo and now leave a big useless gap.
- Build one compact bespoke cobalt-and-ivory moulded nameplate whose stepped/sloping perimeter fits the new two-line wordmark. It should be only as tall as the logo plus comfortable even padding, no empty crown.
- Make the cream letters actual shallow raised enamel/plastic lettering, physically seated into the cobalt panel. Coral red is the visible extruded sidewall material and ties into the console's coral switches. Match bevels, contact shadows, highlight direction and finish to the bottom console. NO flat decal or independent sticker shadow.
- Engineer the mint swoosh as a thin inset luminous light-pipe following the bottom edge of the nameplate, not a free floating brush stroke crossing a frame. Its curved path still matches the approved logo. The little UFO/beam is cleanly inlaid into the A.
- Put RESEARCH CREDITS and NEXT BLUEPRINT in a neatly attached two-window instrument dock directly below the nameplate, with clean margins and enough space. 1,240 and 42 / 60 CAPTURES stay unchanged.
- Header is centered, confidently composed, smaller and tidier than the old frame so more farmland shows. All edges fit screen margins.
Carry that same cream/cobalt/coral/mint material system subtly through the existing bottom console: coral-red destination arrow keys replacing mismatched orange; same moulded bevel profile; crisp consistent cream and navy text. Preserve the big mint START RUN button, LOCATION / FARMLAND selector, HANGAR and SETTINGS controls and their arrangement. Do not add logos elsewhere.
Preserve the supplied low-poly sage farmland scene, barn, trees, farmer, sheep, blue saucer and mint cow-abduction composition, portrait framing, central openness and all existing control labels. Do not copy poster scene content. Output one polished full-screen 850x1850 portrait mockup, no device frame, no comparison board. This needs authored product design and tasteful restraint, not extra decoration.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a convincingly integrated branding revision of the atomic-pulp Human Resources portrait mobile home screen.
IMAGE 1 is the prior unsuccessful integration; IMAGE 2 is the approved poster logo, used only as the logo reference. The last attempt pasted the new wordmark onto an old mismatched sign. Redesign the sign and supporting UI composition around the logo so the result looks intentionally made as one product.

Keep the exact poster wordmark design: HUMAN above RESOURCES, cream angular slanted custom letterforms, exaggerated H and R, coral offset sides, blue saucer / mint triangular beam with star inside the A, curved mint underline. Respect the specific shapes and lockup. No random italic substitute.
NEW INTEGRATED ATOMIC HEADER:
1. Discard the existing oversized skewed rectangular navy billboard with its right-hand wing, old orbit references and random starbursts. Its silhouette does not fit the wordmark.
2. Create a custom die-cut retro enamel sign directly shaped around the new wordmark: a tight stepped contour around its two sloping rows, with even navy breathing room, fine ivory keyline and coral enamel edge. It should follow the logo's actual upward momentum. No giant vacant box or separate background rectangle. Keep a modest shadow so it belongs to the same tactile enamel-sign family as the bottom controls.
3. Make the cream letters painted/embossed into this sign's surface with matching subtle enamel finish and unified highlights; coral sidewalls share the exact colour of the sign trim. The mint swoosh becomes an actual inset luminous strip along the custom sign's lower contour. The little saucer and beam belong to the A. Avoid doubled shadows or floating sticker effects.
4. Center this tailored logo sign near the top, with safe margins and room around the letter tips. It should feel confident and compact rather than an enormous billboard.
5. Move the existing two resource cards into a single aligned supporting row immediately UNDER this header, with balanced width, shared ivory/cobalt enamel treatment and quiet mint accents. Left: 1,240 / RESEARCH CREDITS. Right: NEXT BLUEPRINT / 42 / 60 CAPTURES plus mint progress bar and small blueprint pictogram. No top-corner scattered cards competing above the title.
6. Remove decorative yellow starbursts elsewhere so the poster's coral/mint/ivory/cobalt identity is coherent. Small ordinary specular glints are fine.

Retain the fun vintage saucer-shaped START RUN button at the bottom and the FARMLAND left/right selector above it, plus paired HANGAR and SETTINGS buttons. Refine their edge widths, enamel finish and type treatment to share the logo sign's material language. START RUN stays highly legible cream on cobalt; one restrained coral offset and mint luminous saucer rim echo the logo. Do not repeat the logo or add visual clutter.
Preserve the original low-poly daylight farmland, red barn, trees, farmer, sheep, central blue saucer and glowing mint cow abduction, their framing and relative placement. Keep a generous uninterrupted central scene. No poster night sky, abducted man or houses. Preserve all existing menu functions and sample values.
One polished 850x1850 portrait mobile home screen, no device mockup, no comparison board. It should look like one bespoke game UI, with every trim and typographic choice belonging to the same world.
